text: This chapter's three lessons didn't teach anything new. They built two real scripts and one real near-miss for a single company, Thornfield Analytics, using every chapter this course has taught — which is the only real way to know whether the pieces actually fit together. This final lesson walks through all seven chapters in order and names exactly where each one showed up.

Chapter 1 never taught a cmdlet. It taught the two questions that had to be answered before Lesson 29's cost-savings script could be trusted: is this the right tool for this job, and will it still be safe the thousandth time it runs? That script answered both — PowerShell for an Azure-native task, and a power-state check before ever calling Stop-AzVM, with a try/catch keeping one bad VM from halting the whole loop.

Chapters 2 and 3 gave this course two full toolkits instead of one. Lesson 29 used PowerShell's Az module for an Azure-native operational task. Lesson 30 used Python's Azure SDK instead, specifically because a tag check across every resource type benefits from Python's general-purpose data handling more than it needs PowerShell's Azure-specific cmdlet shape. Same job, two correct answers, picked for the actual task in front of you.

Chapter 4's CLI scripting is the third option for quick, single-purpose jobs that don't justify a full script file. Chapter 5 is the one chapter this capstone's labs didn't use directly, and that's worth naming: Bicep and CloudFormation declare what infrastructure should exist before it's created, while this chapter is about operating infrastructure that already exists — a different question, answered by a different tool.

Chapter 6 named operational tasks worth automating, and Lessons 29 and 30 built two of them for real. Chapter 7 is the thread that ties the whole chapter together: source control, running from a pipeline instead of a laptop, and pipeline-managed secrets are what turned Lesson 30's script from a file on someone's laptop into the nightly check that caught a dangerous tag removal in Lesson 31 before it became a real outage.

That's the full course — from choosing the right tool, to writing idempotent, error-handled scripts in PowerShell and Python, to scripting across two clouds, to previewing infrastructure as code, to automating the operational work that actually eats a cloud team's time, to running all of it from a pipeline instead of a laptop. Course complete. Next up in this path: Cloud Deployment, Monitoring, Backup & Job-Ready Capstone, closing the Job-Ready Foundation stage.
